mechanism_narrative: Strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates robust economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days as corporate earnings prospects improve.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth above the 75th percentile fails to produce positive 60-day forward returns in more than 60% of cases, or the average return is not significantly positive (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Elevated unemployment (UNRATE > 5.0%) signals economic distress, causing investors to reduce equity exposure and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE > 5.0%, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances, or the average return is not significantly negative (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of rising monetary policy (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) and high unemployment (UNRATE > 5.0%) indicates a tightening cycle in a weak labor market, which typically triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary tightening in weak labor market
failure_condition: When both FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and UNRATE > 5.0%, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced liquidity and higher discount rates for equities.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) reflects strong manufacturing activity, which correlates with improved corporate profits and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth above the 75th percentile fails to produce positive 5-day forward returns in more than 60% of cases, or the average return is not significantly positive (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Declining housing starts (HOUST < 2200.0) indicate a weakening housing market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending decline.
failure_condition: When HOUST < 2200.0, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between falling housing starts (HOUST < 2250.0) and rising retail sales (RSAFS > 360000.0) suggests a shift in consumer spending toward non-housing sectors, which typically drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST < 2250.0 and RSAFS > 360000.0, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of weak industrial production (INDPRO < 105.0), the S&P 500 tends to decline over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate output and earnings growth.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 105.0, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.
